rows.after: unresolved: genuinely unreachable in a played life (the US has no cooling-off period in content/accountlife.ts, so inCoolingOff is false for every New Haven account). The New Haven half (no Cancel It, the refusal, the account kept) is proved; abroad the card branch (London), the current-account branch and its refusals are proved, the panel drawn while a refusal holds (the reason under it, Cancel It grayed with the same words), and three defects are fixed: a current account is settled on canceling as Close It settles one (its interest paid, its fees charged, in Canada its fees refunded), each part played abroad. From the later pass of 2026-10-15: canceling follows each country’s rule on interest (kept in Britain and Canada, returned in the EU/EEA countries and Mexico) and on charges (refunded for any deposit account in Canada and Mexico); Korea’s deposits have no cooling-off; and Close It refuses a German account its closing fees would overdraw, as Cancel It does. From that day’s recheck, five more defects fixed abroad: a term’s interest taken during the term is refused back out of a primary that doesn’t hold it (Berlin); Canada’s refund leaves out overdraft interest (Toronto); Canada’s 14 and Mexico’s 10 days are counted as business days, on the panel’s “until” date too (Toronto, Mexico City); Canada’s cards have no cooling-off (Toronto); a Mexican account once used has none (Mexico City). Mexico’s half of both rules and the German interest tax’s reversal are tested. From that day’s second recheck, two more defects fixed abroad: a term’s taken interest is found by the term itself, not by the name every term at the bank shares, so canceling a new Deutsche Bank term no longer takes back an older one’s (Berlin); and the period runs to the end of its last day, as each rule counts it, not to the hour the account opened (Toronto, Berlin). The refusal’s one-cent threshold is tested. Each FIXTURE, as no played life banks outside the US.
rows.disposition: stale-claim (unreachable by design); implementation fixed (engine and missing control); evidence complete abroad

fixes.summary: Canceling kept a savings account’s or term deposit’s interest from it everywhere, and paid a current account’s everywhere. It follows the country’s rule now: kept in Britain and Canada; returned, any already paid posted back with its tax and off the year’s income, in the EU/EEA countries and Mexico.
Canada’s refund of charges covered only a current account; it covers any deposit account now, and Mexico’s with it.
Korea’s deposits had a 14-day cooling-off its rule (금융소비자보호법 제46조) doesn’t give; removed, cards kept.
Close It closed a German account overdrawn by its closing fees; refused now, as Cancel It refuses it.

A term’s interest taken during the term (bank.take_term_interest) went into the primary account, and Cancel It took it back out of there, but cancelRefusal counted only interest paid into the term itself, so nothing refused it and a Commerzbank primary was left at −€6.30 (Postbank −€6.08). interestBackOf now counts each payment by the holder’s account it went into, and cancelRefusal refuses while any of those holds less than goes back out of it. Deutsche Bank’s own terms say only that each side repays what it received within 30 days (its ZinsMarkt Widerrufsfolgen), nothing of keeping it back from the deposit, so it’s refused rather than taken from the term.

fixes.summary: A Canadian card had a 14-day cooling-off. Bank Act s.627.11 lets a credit card agreement be canceled “in accordance with any prescribed requirements”, and SOR/2021-181 prescribes them for a retail deposit account (s.5), a deposit-type instrument (s.6) and the products s.4 lists, no card among them (read 2026-10-15). inCoolingOff is false for a Canadian card.

fixes.summary: Mexico’s right holds only “siempre y cuando el Cliente no haya utilizado u operado los productos o servicios financieros contratados” (art. 11 Bis 1, read 2026-10-15 at diputados.gob.mx, last reform 14 November 2025); SLATE didn’t ask. SLATE can tell: usedSince counts a payment out of the account by its holder, a card’s purchase among them, and not the bank’s fees, its interest or its tax; money paid in isn’t counted, an account being funded to be opened (SLATE’s reading). A used Mexican account is out of its cooling-off.

Interest taken before the fix carries no such posting and isn’t found on canceling (in a save from before it, that interest gets no refusal and no reversal).

fixes.summary: The cooling-off period ended at the hour the account opened on its last day (openedAt + days, or afterBusinessDays at the same hour), though Directive 2002/65/EC art. 6(1) gives 14 calendar days, SOR/2021-181 s.5(1) “within 14 business days after the day on which [it] is opened”, and LTOSF art. 11 Bis 1 “diez días hábiles posteriores”, and the panel named the day: an RBC account “until January 23” was refused at 11:30 AM on the 23rd. coolingOffEnds returns the last moment of that day in the save’s zone (endOfDay), and the panel names the date in that zone.

tutorial: bank (Your Bank): its account-life sentence was changed on 2026-10-15’s recheck, that sentence alone, to “Where the country has a cooling-off period, a new account or card other than your primary can be canceled within it: in Korea a card alone, in Canada no card, in Britain no fixed-rate deposit, and in Mexico only one not yet used.” It had said any new savings account, term deposit, card or current account, untrue of Korea since the Korea fix.

recheck.problem: No test drew the panel while a current account’s refusal held (the reason under it, Cancel It grayed out), as the row text and guide/money.ts:527 said.

recheck.problem: The checking branch skipped Close It’s interest and fee settlement while guide/money.ts:506 said a current account “closes the same way”.
recheck.done: Chose the code, after reading the rules: Britain’s FCA BCOBS 6.3.2R (the customer pays for the service actually provided, proportionate), Germany’s BGB § 357b(2) (Wertersatz for the service provided), and Canada’s SOR/2021-181 s.5(2) (closed without charge, the operation’s charges refunded, interest charges aside). The account’s earned interest is the holder’s, so paying it charges nothing anywhere. bank.cancel_new now settles interest and fees as closeNow does and clears the limit; in Canada it refunds the fees charged while it was open; fees past what it holds are refused (cancelRefusal, read by the panel too). Tested in Toronto, Berlin and Reykjavík with hand-worked literals; each part’s mutation fails its test. Guide :506 and :527 and the panel’s words now say what happens.

recheck.problem: Cancel It’s savings and term-deposit branch paid no interest earned in the window.
recheck.done: Each country’s rule read (BCOBS 6.3.2R and Nationwide’s terms, SOR/2021-181 s.5, Directive 2002/65/EC art. 7, BGB § 355(3), LTOSF art. 11 Bis 1): kept in Britain and Canada, returned in the EU/EEA countries and Mexico, for every account canceled. London, Berlin Flexgeld and Reykjavík test it; defects5’s RBC term literal moved to $4,000.26 by hand.

recheck.problem: A Canadian savings withdrawal fee charged in the window wasn’t refunded.
recheck.done: Refunded for any deposit account in Canada (and Mexico, whose rule forbids any commission); Toronto RBC savings test.

recheck.problem: Korea’s deposit cooling-off.
recheck.done: Removed: 제46조 gives 청약철회 to insurance, investment and lending products only. Guide names Korea for cards alone; past-tense comments in accountlife.ts and guide/money.ts. Seoul test.

recheck.problem: Close It could close a German account its fees overdrew.
recheck.done: closeRefusal refuses it, the panel graying Close It with the words; Berlin Close It test.

recheck.problem: Abroad fix 1: a term deposit’s interest taken during the term (Take Interest) went back out of the primary on Cancel It, but interestBackOf counted only postings on the term, so no refusal fired; a Commerzbank primary was left at −€6.30 (Postbank −€6.08).
recheck.done: Fixed in accountlife.ts: interestBackOf counts each payment by the holder’s account it went into; cancelRefusal refuses while any of them holds less, “The interest it paid into GiroKonto, €6.30, goes back out of it, and is more than it holds. Pay in €6.30 first.”. Checked the bank’s terms first: Deutsche Bank’s ZinsMarkt pre-contract information (Widerrufsfolgen) says each side returns what it received within 30 days, nothing of keeping it back from the deposit, so it’s refused, not taken from the term. Tested: FIXTURE, Berlin, Commerzbank primary and a Deutsche Bank FestzinsSparen, €6.30 worked by hand (10,000 × 0.023 × 10 / 365), the panel and the command refused, then canceled with the primary at €0.00; failed before (went through). Guide unavailable line added.

recheck.problem: Abroad fix 2: Canada’s refund took every bank_fee transaction, overdraft interest among them, against SOR/2021-181 s.5(2)(b) “other than interest charges”, and credited all of it against Bank Fees.
recheck.done: Fixed in accountlife.ts: chargesBackOf leaves out a charge against the Overdraft Interest line and returns each charge by its expense line, which the refund credits. Tested: FIXTURE, Toronto: C$16.95 + C$5.00 = C$21.95 refunded against Bank Fees, the C$1.81 of interest ((5 × 500 + 516.95) × 0.22 / 365) kept; failed before (C$23.76). Every refundable charge the game makes is on Bank Fees, so the line-by-line credit changes no outcome today and no test can tell it from one Bank Fees posting; it’s a guard for a charge on another line. Guide outcome line says overdraft interest isn’t refunded.

recheck.problem: Mexico’s entries in REFUNDS_CHARGES and KEEPS_INTEREST were reached by no test.
recheck.done: Two FIXTURE tests in Mexico City: a Banorte saver’s MXN 42.46 (1,000,000 × 0.0031 × 5 / 365) posted back on canceling, and a Santander LikeU’s MXN 11.48 refunded, with the panel’s words “its money back without the interest it earned, and its fees refunded.”. Removing MX from REFUNDS_CHARGES or adding it to KEEPS_INTEREST fails them (run). The Santander charge is posted by hand: SLATE charges its quiet-month fee only for a whole month open, and no Mexican bank here charges an unused account inside its ten business days, so no charge the game makes reaches the refund; the test says so.

recheck.problem: Canada’s 14 business days and Mexico’s 10 días hábiles were counted as calendar days; Mexico’s right needs the product unused; SOR/2021-181 gives Canada’s cards no cooling-off right.
recheck.done: All three fixed. coolingOffEnds counts Canada’s and Mexico’s with afterBusinessDays (inCoolingOff and the panel’s “until” date read it); tests/accountlife.test.ts re-dated with a dated comment (in the period eighteen days on, refused nineteen), and the Mexico City Banorte test cancels on 10 February, past ten calendar days. Read SOR/2021-181 in full on 2026-10-15: s.627.11 of the Bank Act covers a card “in accordance with any prescribed requirements”, and the regulation prescribes none for a card; inCoolingOff is false for a Canadian card, and the card test moved to London (Consumer Credit Act s.66A) with Toronto’s RBC card refused. Mexico: SLATE can tell use, as a payment out by the holder (fees, interest and tax aside; money in not counted, SLATE’s reading); a used Mexican account is out of its period, tested with a twin that sent MXN 100 out.

abroad.finding: Cancel It’s savings and term-deposit branch paid no interest earned in the window, in every country; and its current-account branch paid the interest in every country.
abroad.source: Britain: FCA BCOBS 6.3.2R (handbook.fca.org.uk/handbook/BCOBS/6/3.html, read 2026-10-15), only the service actually provided, never a penalty; Nationwide Savings Account Terms P2797 (January 2026) condition 76, “will not deduct any interest you have earned to date” (read 2026-10-15). Canada: SOR/2021-181 s.5 (lois-laws.justice.gc.ca, read 2026-10-15), closed “without charge”, silent on interest earned. EU/EEA: Directive 2002/65/EC art. 7(4)-(5) (legislation.gov.uk/eudr/2002/65/article/7, read 2026-10-15), the consumer returns any sums received from the supplier; Germany BGB § 355(3) (gesetze-im-internet.de, read 2026-10-15) and Deutsche Bank’s ZinsMarkt-Festgeld pre-contract information (February 2025), “die beiderseits empfangenen Leistungen zurückzugewähren”. Mexico: LTOSF art. 11 Bis 1 (cnbv.gob.mx, as amended to 24 January 2024, read 2026-10-15), things returned “al estado en el que se encontraban antes de su firma”. Iceland’s lög 33/2005: althingi.is refused the fetch; taken as the directive it transposes.
abroad.fix: src/engine/systems/accountlife.ts: KEEPS_INTEREST (GB, CA) settles the interest on canceling for any account; elsewhere (the EU/EEA countries, Mexico) the interest building is dropped and any paid since opening is posted back with its tax, and taken off the year’s income record (interestPaidSince, recordInterest negative). cancelRefusal counts the interest going back toward what the account must hold. The panel’s words come from cancelWords (BankAccountLife.tsx); guide/money.ts’s Cancel It line rewritten, with a past-tense comment.

abroad.finding: Canada refunds the charges on any retail deposit account canceled, savings among them, and a savings withdrawal fee charged in the window wasn’t refunded.
abroad.source: SOR/2021-181 s.5(2)(b): “refund any charges related to the operation of the retail deposit account, other than interest charges, that are incurred while the account was open” (lois-laws.justice.gc.ca/eng/regulations/SOR-2021-181/FullText.html, read 2026-10-15). Mexico’s LTOSF art. 11 Bis 1, “no podrán cobrar Comisión alguna”, read the same day, makes the same so there.

abroad.finding: Close It could close a German account whose closing fees exceeded its balance, leaving it overdrawn, where Cancel It refused the same account.
abroad.source: SLATE’s own rule in closeRefusal, that the bank closes an overdrawn account only once that’s paid; Germany’s fees are settled at closing (settleFees, the quarter so far). No bank term was read for this: the decision is the consistency with the refusal already there.
abroad.fix: src/engine/systems/bankmoves.ts closeRefusal: refused when the fees closing charges exceed what it holds with its interest, net of tax: “Its fees, …, are more than it holds. Pay in … first.” Your Banks grays Close It with the words as its title, and the command refuses. guide/money.ts’s Close It conditions and refusals list it, with a past-tense comment.

abroad.finding: Found while reading the sources, not fixed: Canada’s period is 14 business days after the day the account is opened (SOR/2021-181 s.5(1)) and Mexico’s ten días hábiles (LTOSF art. 11 Bis 1), where SLATE counts 14 and 10 calendar days; and Mexico’s right holds only while the product hasn’t been used or operated, which SLATE doesn’t ask. SOR/2021-181 has no 14-day right for a credit card, which SLATE gives Canada’s cards.
abroad.fix: Not fixed in this pass: business days would change inCoolingOff, the panel’s “until” date and tests/accountlife.test.ts’s fifteen-day refusal, outside the four findings; content/bankdays.ts’s afterBusinessDays already counts a country’s business days.
